data.label: Synthetic user (browser)
data.description: Synthetic test user chatting through a browser. This is a client reference and isn't provisioned.

data.label: Sign-in
data.description: Signs users in and issues tokens. The app validates the token and uses the user's object ID as the conversation partition key. Tenant and user flow aren't chosen yet.

data.label: Chat application
data.description: Web UI and chat orchestration. It validates tokens, loads the user's recent turns, enforces a context budget (recent turns plus a summary), calls the model, runs safety checks and decides when to escalate. It returns the reply to the user. It takes no external actions. It uses managed identity to reach downstream services.

data.label: Conversation state
data.description: Per-user conversation history, partitioned by user ID. The app only reads and writes the caller's own partition. Retention isn't decided yet.

data.label: Model runtime
data.description: Chat model deployment. The model, region, quota and access are still to be verified. Local tests use scripted mock responses instead.

data.label: Safety check
data.description: Screens user input and model output. Flagged items trigger refusal or escalation.

data.label: Escalation queue
data.description: Holds escalation tickets (conversation reference and reason) for human review, with a dead-letter queue. The escalation trigger and owner are still open.

data.label: Human reviewer
data.description: The person who handles escalated conversations. This is outside the provisioning scope.

data.label: Monitoring and audit
data.description: Traces, errors, latency, token usage and escalation events. Prompt content is excluded from logs by default.

Explain the first local test, distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation, and ask one useful missing-decision question. Do not reduce this application to storage to satisfy generator coverage. Do not invent successful deployment or approved region/account access.

decisions.subject: design.azure-authenticated-conversational-assistant-first-sketch
decisions.title: Azure authenticated conversational assistant (first sketch)
decisions.context: Scope: authenticated chat for synthetic users with per-user conversation state, a model runtime, a bounded context window, a safety check and escalation to a person. External actions are excluded. Assumptions: the region, model, account access and quotas aren't chosen or verified yet. Managed identity is assumed between services. No native Terraform generator exists for this Azure workload yet, so engineering work is required. Local tests use a mocked model and don't prove model quality, identity and access control, or deployment.
decisions.decision: Drawn while talking as design revision 2.

needs.statement: Proposed: only authenticated users can chat, and each user can read or continue only their own conversation history. Requests without a valid token are rejected.
needs.rationale: If conversations leak between users, it's a privacy breach. This rule fails closed when identity is missing.
needs.basis: User: "authenticated conversational assistant" with "per-user conversation state".

needs.statement: Proposed: each model call includes only a bounded context (recent turns plus a summary) within a configurable token budget.
needs.rationale: Without a limit, long conversations push up cost, slow responses and eventually exceed the model's limits. The token value isn't set yet.

needs.statement: Proposed: the assistant escalates qualifying conversations to a human review queue without taking any external actions. The trigger and owner are still to be confirmed.
needs.rationale: If the assistant gets stuck or hits a sensitive case, there needs to be a safe exit. If nobody owns the queue, escalations go unanswered.
needs.basis: User: "an escalation path. No external actions in this first test."
